newsitem.title: UK: Still unclear who to pay windfall tax - UK minister.
newsitem.headline: Still unclear who to pay windfall tax - UK minister.

text.p: A British treasury minister said on Thursday the Labour Party had still failed to make it clear who would pay its planned windfall tax on privatised utilities.
Labour economic spokesman Gordon Brown said earlier he had legal advice that the tax could not be challenged in the courts.
But Financial Secretary to the Treasury Ian Jack said Brown had been unable in interviews on this announcement to answer the key question of which companies would be caught by the tax.
"He was unable to define what he meant by a utility. He was frightened to admit who would be affected," Jack said in a statement.

Jack said the companies which might, or might not, be affected by the tax included British Airways, British Telecommunications, railway companies and water companies which have never been in the public sector.
